headline_marked: [[Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches]] November 5th for Nintendo Switch 2, with modern updates
headline: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches November 5th for Nintendo Switch 2, with modern updates
summary: The game will feature a dedicated jump button, full voice acting, and a 'Threads of Time' progression tracker, alongside a new visual style inspired by puppet shows.
details: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches November 5th for Nintendo Switch 2. Physical editions are initially available for $59.99, but will likely increase to $69.99 post-launch, while the digital version remains at $59.99.

The remake features a much more realistic visual style, inspired by puppet shows, creating a convincing sense of character existence within fantasy worlds. Art director Aya Shida explained this approach aims to evoke the distinctive nostalgia of the original game.

Modern improvements include a dedicated jump button, a sprint ability, and full voice acting. Despite these changes, many elements remain faithful to the classic Nintendo 64 release, including the ability to spam the Roll Attack.

Nintendo added features like 'Threads of Time,' a new progression marker viewable when paused, and Zelda Notes integration within the Nintendo Switch app for maps and info. These additions aim to make the game more welcoming to players familiar with modern Zelda titles like Breath of the Wild.

To celebrate the launch, Nintendo is also releasing a special version of the Switch 2 and a Switch 2 Pro Controller adorned with Triforce imagery. Additionally, Hori has listed a $49.99 electronic ocarina that can be used with the remake's sound recognition feature.

topic: gaming mod sites implement ai disclosure policy
headline_marked: [[Nexus Mods makes AI disclosure mandatory]] for all new mod uploads, 60-day grace period for existing ones
headline: Nexus Mods makes AI disclosure mandatory for all new mod uploads, 60-day grace period for existing ones
summary: The PC gaming modding platform Nexus Mods now requires authors to declare if AI was used in their work, aiming for transparency rather than an outright ban on AI-generated content.
details: Nexus Mods, a major PC gaming mods repository, has announced that authors of all newly uploaded mods must declare "whether AI has been used in their work." This new policy is part of a broader stance on AI-generated content on the platform.

The site will not implement an outright ban on AI-generated mods, citing the difficulty in drawing clear boundaries for AI use across the entire creation process. Instead, the focus is on transparency, ensuring AI use is "out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated."

Mods tagged as "AI-assisted" will also be required to include a public explanation of how and where AI was utilized. These AI tags will be made more prominent on mod pages to provide clearer information to users.

Nexus Mods has stated it is "pro-human creativity" and will neither use mods to train AI nor sell or license them to anyone doing so. The platform is also working on clearer controls for mod reuse and strengthening attribution for derivative works.

Beyond AI, Nexus Mods is addressing issues with rapid mod uploads by single authors, which can push other content down the "Recently Added" section. Changes include limits on how many mods from one author are shown at a time and tighter restrictions for new accounts.

The platform is also rolling out controls to hide AI-generated content on game pages and the homepage, with similar functionality planned for search results. This gives users more control over the content they see.

Mod authors have a 60-day grace period to update their existing mods to meet the new requirements, with enforcement beginning on January 2nd. The full AI policy is available on the Nexus Mods website.
